translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Wharton’s ironic, balanced periodic narration and her free indirect style through Newland Archer are kept without softening or explanation.
decisions.rationale: The novel’s effect is the irony toward the tribe’s code and Archer’s own blindness.

decisions.decision: The source’s straight quotation marks are rendered as typographic curly quotes, with the same number of marks per unit.
decisions.rationale: Standard Vietnamese typography; the count is checked against the source.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Mr. van der Luyden addressed Archer with a female term (‘cô’); now ‘cậu’.
‘Our cousin’ is the Duke, but the draft made it a female cousin; corrected.
‘Episcopalian’ was rendered with the Methodist term; now the Episcopal Church.
‘Husband of Ellen Olenska’s cousin’ read as Ellen’s own husband; corrected.
‘Don’t you always know what to say?’ became a question that inverted the sense; corrected.

The first slice used ‘chàng’ for Archer and ‘nàng’ for May and Ellen while the other slices used ‘anh’, ‘cô’ and ‘bà’; unified across the book (the epithets ‘nàng Cassandra’ and ‘nàng Pocahontas’ were kept).

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: Thời đại ngây thơ; Quyển I; Quyển II
glossary.rationale: Titles are translated; chapter numerals are kept.

glossary.draft_rendering: anh / cô / bà (Ellen) — with ‘nàng’ and ‘chàng’ avoided
glossary.rationale: One address system through the book.

glossary.draft_rendering: bà Olenska / nữ bá tước Olenska
glossary.rationale: Formal reference for the married Countess.

witness_decision: Selected Project Gutenberg #541, an electronic transcription of The Age of Innocence by Edith Wharton (1920). The text was not collated with the first printing.

unresolved_questions.explanation: ‘The tribe’ is rendered ‘bộ tộc’ in some places and ‘bộ lạc’ in the glossary.
The register of ‘hắn’ in units 636–659 is rougher than the surrounding narration.

title_review.rationale: The title is translated as ‘Thời đại ngây thơ’; no earlier Vietnamese title was checked.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The opening: the opera evening in January, in the Academy of Music.
The last unit: ‘Newland Archer got up slowly and walked back alone to his hotel.’
